Temporal graph network with node memory

Source: R/tgn.R
tgn_model.Rd

A memory based model for continuous time dynamic link prediction in the style of TGN (Rossi et al. 2020). Every node keeps a memory vector that a GRU updates whenever the node takes part in an event. Events are processed in chronological batches:

Usage

tgn_model(
  num_nodes,
  memory_dim = 32L,
  time_dim = 16L,
  embedding_dim = 32L,
  edge_dim = 0L,
  embedding = c("time", "graph_sum", "graph_attention"),
  num_neighbors = 10L,
  node_embedding = TRUE,
  heads = 2L
)

train_tgn(
  model,
  split,
  epochs = 10L,
  batch_size = 200L,
  lr = 0.001,
  seed = NULL,
  device = NULL
)

Arguments

num_nodes

Number of nodes.

memory_dim

Memory size.

time_dim

Size of the time encoding.

embedding_dim

Embedding size.

edge_dim

Number of event features (0 for none).

embedding

"time", "graph_sum" or "graph_attention".

num_neighbors

Most recent partners used by the graph embeddings.

node_embedding

Add a learned static embedding per node to \(z_i\) (useful without node features; makes the model transductive).

heads

Attention heads for "graph_attention"; embedding_dim must be divisible by it.

model

A tgn_model.

split

Result of split_temporal() (train, val, test).

epochs

Passes over the training events.

batch_size

Events per batch. A batch is extended so it never splits events that share a timestamp; those are scored together before any of them updates the memory.

lr

Learning rate.

seed

Optional seed for weights, negatives and the epoch order. Each event gets one random negative destination that differs from its own source and destination. The three periods of split must follow each other in time.

device

Device.

Value

tgn_model(): an nn_module.

train_tgn(): a temporal_fit with history, val_metrics and test_metrics (ROC AUC and average precision against one random destination per event). Evaluation continues the memory built over the training (and, for test, validation) events, without gradient updates.

Details

  1. The raw messages of the previous batch update the memory of the nodes involved (message \([s_i, s_j, \phi(t - t_i^{last}), e_{ij}]\), keeping the most recent message per node, then \(s_i \leftarrow \mathrm{GRU}(m_i, s_i)\)). Doing this at the start of the next batch lets gradients reach the GRU while the current batch's own events never inform its predictions.

  2. Node embeddings are computed from memory and the time since the node's last update, \(z_i = W [s_i, \phi(t - t_i^{last})]\) (embedding = "time"), plus, with embedding = "graph_sum", the mean of \(W' [s_j, \phi(t - t_{ij})]\) over the num_neighbors most recent earlier interaction partners \(j\). With embedding = "graph_attention" (the paper's best variant), multi head attention runs over those partners with query \(W_Q [s_i, \phi(0)]\), keys and values \(W_{K,V} [s_j, \phi(t - t_{ij}), e_{ij}]\), and \(z_i = \mathrm{MLP}([\tilde h_i, s_i, \phi(t - t_i^{last})])\), \(\tilde h_i\) the attention output (zero without partners); the weights of the last call are kept in model$last_attention.

  3. An MLP scores \([z_{src}, z_{dst}]\); the loss is binary cross entropy against one random destination per event.

\(\phi(\Delta t) = \cos(\omega \Delta t + b)\) is the learnable time encoding of TGAT (Xu et al. 2020). Memory is detached between batches (truncated backpropagation over one batch). Only one embedding layer (one hop) and the "last" message aggregator are implemented.

References

Rossi, Chamberlain, Frasca, Eynard, Monti and Bronstein (2020) Temporal graph networks for deep learning on dynamic graphs. Xu, Ruan, Korpeoglu, Kumar and Achan (2020) Inductive representation learning on temporal graphs.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  tg <- dataset_synthetic_temporal(seed = 1)
  sp <- split_temporal(tg)
  m <- tgn_model(tg$num_nodes, memory_dim = 16, embedding_dim = 16)
  fit <- train_tgn(m, sp, epochs = 2, batch_size = 100, seed = 1)
  fit$test_metrics
}
#>           roc_auc average_precision 
#>         0.4997609         0.5301846
